title: Senior Demand Strategy Lead, Experiences
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join: 

The Experiences team is responsible for scaling a curated, high-quality supply of unique activities hosted by local creators, iconic businesses, and operators worldwide and we're at an inflection point. 

We have a large and growing captive audience of guests who have booked or are considering a trip, and a suite of lifecycle, CRM, and owned-content levers that remain significantly under-optimized. Email, push, transactional messaging, and our owned editorial channels are low-cost, high-reach ways to move demand once the right strategy, testing infrastructure, and automation are in place.

The Difference You Will Make:

As a Senior Demand Strategy Lead, you are entrusted with owning the strategy end to end, defining how we engage guests across the full lifecycle, from discovery and booking through post-experience engagement and repeat, and how owned content builds demand alongside it. You set the direction, define success metrics, identify what is and isn't working, and own the outcome. Where Growth Marketing is accountable for shipping the work, you're accountable for whether it actually moves demand: this is a senior, broad mandate, where you own a priority outright and set strategy that XFN partners and vendors execute against, rather than running campaigns yourself. This role reports to the Director of Global Demand for Experiences. 

A Typical Day: 

Own lifecycle & CRM strategy

  • Define the end-to-end guest lifecycle strategy for Experiences, from first touch through repeat booking
  • Own the roadmap for email and push programs: Tripcycle, home-abandoner sequences, transactional messaging, and Launchpad integration
  • Identify the highest-impact audience segments, messaging angles, and send cadences, and build a rigorous testing framework to validate them
  • Drive automation of high-performing sends to maximize reach with minimal ongoing cost

Own editorial & owned content

  • Set the strategy for the Experiences newsletter and other owned content we produce: what we publish, to whom, and how it ties to demand and discovery
  • Build an editorial calendar and a content-to-conversion measurement approach, so owned content is held to demand outcomes, not just engagement
  • Partner with Brand, Creative, and the affiliates/social lead so owned content, social, and lifecycle reinforce one another rather than overlap

Own Guest Referrals program strategy

  • Define the strategy and success criteria for the Experiences guest referral program
  • Partner with Product on UX improvements and bonus design to drive adoption
  • Track performance and iterate on incentive structures to find the lever that moves the needle

Drive XFN execution

  • Partner with Growth Marketing and Engineering to translate strategy into shipped campaigns and automated workflows
  • Maintain a clear view of what is in flight, blocked, or needs escalation, with a regular reporting cadence
  • Influence Product roadmap prioritization so lifecycle and content capabilities keep pace with strategy

Your Expertise:

  • 12+ years in growth, lifecycle, CRM, email, or content marketing, ideally in a consumer marketplace or travel context
  • Track record owning a channel or lifecycle strategy end to end and being accountable for its business outcome, not just executing campaigns
  • Experience setting strategy that others (XFN partners, agencies, or a small team) execute against, in a matrixed environment
  • Strong analytical skills: builds measurement frameworks, interprets A/B tests, uses data to drive decisions
  • Experience building and scaling email/push automation programs
  • Editorial or owned-content judgment: can shape what we say and publish, not only how we send it
  • Crisp written and verbal communication: writes clear briefs, presents strategy to leadership, aligns stakeholders

Nice to have

  • Two-sided marketplace or platform experience with both supply and demand levers
  • Familiarity with marketing automation platforms and referral/incentive mechanics
  • Experience running a newsletter or editorial program with a measurable growth mandate

descriptionHtml:

The BizTech BI&Analytics team partners with business and finance stakeholders to deliver scalable self-serve analytics & AI transformation programs, budgeting & forecasting solutions, reliable data pipelines, and trusted metrics & dashboards. Empowering timely, compliant, data-driven decisions and a robust analytics foundation across Airbnb.

The Difference You Will Make:

We are seeking a skilled Senior Systems Engineer to support our Oracle EPM Planning systems and processes, with a strong focus on bringing AI automation and AI agent capabilities into Finance workflows. This is an important role within the Airbnb BizTech organization supporting Finance. The ideal candidate combines solid technical depth in the Finance Budgeting and Forecasting function with hands-on experience building AI automation and AI agents. Responsibilities include financial forecast modeling, system and AI-driven process transformation, integration with the data warehouse, and translating business requirements into scalable Oracle EPM and AI-enabled solutions.

A Typical Day:

Technical Support & System Admin

  • Application: Support the design, configuration, and maintenance of Oracle EPM Planning modules (Financials, Workforce, Capital, Cash Forecast, Long Range Planning, etc).
  • Calculations & Modeling: Develop and maintain business rules and calc scripts. Proficiency in Groovy Scripting for data and forecast modeling.
  • Data Integration: Support data flows with AWS data warehouse, Oracle ERP Cloud, and Workday, leveraging Data Management, EPM Automate, and internal Airbnb integration tools.
  • Environment Management: Assist with the monthly Oracle patch cycle, including regression testing and impact analysis of new features.

FP&A Functional Support

title: Staff Workday Integration Engineer, Tech Foundations
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

About the Team

The Talent Systems team within BizTech is the trusted technology partner to Employee Experience, Recruiting, Payroll, Procurement, Legal, and Privacy teams across Airbnb’s global operations. Driven by the philosophy of “High Tech, Human Touch,” we design and implement technology that meets both business objectives and employee needs: building robust frameworks that support the full employee journey, delivering AI-enabled self-service tools, and playing a key role in payroll management and benefits enrollment.

We own and operate a portfolio of 300+ production integrations and custom applications spanning payroll processors, benefits carriers, identity providers, compliance vendors, and internal platforms, with Workday at the center. We are also building the agentic layer on top of that portfolio: an Airbnb-owned Workday MCP server and AI assistant plugins that let employees and managers act on HR data directly from the tools they already use. You will partner closely with our Systems Architect, HR Centers of Excellence, IT Security, Finance, and external vendors to deliver enterprise-grade integrations and AI-enabled tooling that power Airbnb’s global HR technology ecosystem.

The Difference You Will Make

As a Staff Workday Integration Engineer, you are the technical authority for the integration initiatives that BizTech and Airbnb depend on. You will define our integration strategy and technical roadmap, set the architectural standards other engineers build against, and own the engineering of the Workday MCP and agentic integrations that are reshaping how employees interact with HR processes.

This is a hands-on builder role. You will personally write integration logic, own production reliability, and make the architectural decisions that keep HR data flowing correctly across our global employee population. You will drive touchless automation, reduce manual intervention, and ensure compliance across multiple jurisdictions. Your work directly impacts how thousands of Airbnb employees experience their payroll, benefits, time tracking, and HR processes.

You work alongside a Systems Architect who owns Talent Systems business process architecture, functional design, and the capability roadmap. You need enough functional fluency to build integrations and AI tools that are correct, and the engineering depth to make them reliable. As a Staff-level engineer, you will think 12+ months ahead, proactively surface systemic gaps, mentor the engineers around you, and establish patterns adopted across the Talent Systems team.

What You’ll Own

Integration Architecture & Technical Strategy

  • Define and own Airbnb’s Workday integration architecture standards, patterns, and governance frameworks
  • Lead architectural decisions for complex, high-risk integration initiatives, including global rollouts, payroll runs, benefits open enrollment, and system migrations
  • Evaluate and advise on build-vs-buy decisions, Workday-native-vs-middleware trade-offs, and long-term integration platform strategy
  • Establish reusable integration design patterns, error handling and retry frameworks, and observability standards adopted team-wide
  • Anticipate platform evolution and architect integrations that accommodate Workday’s semi-annual releases with minimal rework
  • Identify and remediate technical debt across the integration landscape: functionality, performance, error handling, and scalability

Core Workday Integration Development

  • Architect, design, build, and maintain complex inbound and outbound integrations using Workday Studio, Core Connectors, EIBs, Document Transforms, and RaaS API endpoints
  • Develop integrations against Workday Web Services (WWS): WSDL interpretation, web service versioning, request/response handling for SOAP and REST
  • Own design and delivery of high-volume integration scenarios: payroll runs, benefits open enrollment, global workforce changes, and multi-country rollouts
  • Own Workday payroll interfaces (PECI, PICOF) and their interaction with third-party payroll providers
  • Build and maintain advanced Custom Reports and Calculated Fields for integration and AI-tool consumption
  • Work within the Business Process Framework, understanding how process events trigger integration flows
  • Build and maintain Workday Extend applications (data models, business logic, UI pages, Extend REST APIs) when Extend is the right tool versus Studio, EIB, or middleware; Extend adoption strategy and SME ownership sit with the Systems Architect
  • Apply Workday Orchestrate for multi-system workflow coordination where it fits
  • Manage the integration portfolio across Workday’s semi-annual release cycle: assess release notes, lead sandbox testing, deploy to production with rigorous change controls

AI & Agentic Integration

  • Own the engineering of Airbnb’s Workday MCP server and its tool surface: tool design, per-user OAuth 2.0 authorization, human-in-the-loop gates on write actions, idempotent write contracts, rate and volume guardrails, and audit logging
  • Design and build agentic integrations that let AI assistant plugins and other enterprise LLM tooling read from and act on Workday safely, with permissions resolved as the authenticated user and no shared service-account fallback for user-attributable actions
  • Co-own the Talent Systems AI architecture and governance framework with the Systems Architect: how agentic tools, Workday-native AI, and enterprise LLM capabilities interconnect, and the guardrails that govern their adoption
  • Evaluate Workday-native agentic capabilities (Agent Ready Tools, MCP Explorer, Workday Agents) and emerging HR AI platforms; provide structured build-vs-buy-vs-configure analysis
  • Translate business use cases into AI tool architectures that are operationally feasible, permission-safe, and measurable
  • Instrument AI tooling for usage and cost (per-tool call metrics) to inform Workday platform entitlement and licensing decisions

Production Reliability, Security & Platform Governance

  • Drive operational excellence across the integration portfolio: SLAs, prioritization, and escalation handling
  • Own SLAs for the most critical integrations and AI tools; establish monitoring, alerting, reconciliation, and runbook standards that raise the bar across the team
  • Drive root cause analysis on integration failures and implement preventative controls
  • Own security, compliance, and governance from the integration and engineering perspective: PII handling, audit controls, and data reconciliation strategies that meet GDPR, SOC 2, SOX, and applicable data privacy requirements for HR data flows
  • Enforce authentication and transport security across all integration surfaces: OAuth 2.0 (including user-context flows), SAML, and secure file transfer (PGP, SFTP)
  • Assess system impacts and risks when introducing new integrations, AI tools, or platform changes, and communicate them clearly before promotion to production
  • Own tenant deployment strategy: sandbox-to-production promotion, Git-based version control of integration and Extend artifacts, CI-friendly testing, and rollback planning

HR Technology & Functional Fluency

  • Maintain a strong working understanding of core HR and payroll processes (hire-to-retire, compensation cycles, benefits enrollment, time and absence, compliance reporting) sufficient to design integrations and AI tools that reflect real business requirements
  • Understand how HR data flows across the enterprise: from Workday as the system of record through downstream payroll processors, benefits carriers, identity providers, and compliance platforms
  • Proactively surface configuration and upstream data issues that affect integration reliability, and partner with the Systems Architect and functional owners to resolve them
  • Bring an employee-centric lens to integration and AI tool design so the technology we build translates to seamless experiences for the people it serves

Technical Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence

  • Act as the technical authority for Workday integrations and HR agentic tooling across BizTech; influence architectural decisions in adjacent teams including Enterprise Integrations, Identity, Data Platform, and AI Products
  • Mentor and upskill senior and mid-level engineers through design reviews, code reviews, pair development, and documented standards
  • Partner with Employee Experience, Recruiting, Payroll, Total Rewards, Legal/Privacy, IT Security, and enterprise architecture to translate ambiguous requirements into sound technical architectures; communicate constraints, trade-offs, and risks at all levels
  • Write authoritative Integration Design Documents, MCP tool specifications, and operational runbooks maintainable by the broader team
  • Proactively identify systemic risks and portfolio health issues; drive resolution and communicate transparently with leadership
  • Represent Talent Systems in enterprise architecture forums, AI tooling quality reviews, and vendor technical discussions; maintain active knowledge of the Workday roadmap and HR technology trends

Your Expertise

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 9+ years of experience in enterprise technology, software development, or systems integration, with at least 5–6 years of hands-on Workday integration development covering the full lifecycle: requirements, design, build, testing, go-live, and post-production support
  • Workday Integration Proficiency (personally written code required):
    • Workday Studio: complex multi-step integrations, sub-integrations, custom error handling and fault frameworks, XSLT transformations
    • Core Connectors and EIBs: worker data, business process events, payroll and benefits outbound connectors; clear judgment on EIB use cases and limitations versus Studio; Document Transform payload mapping
    • Payroll interfaces: PECI and PICOF, and their interaction with third-party payroll providers
    • RaaS (Report-as-a-Service): advanced report design, calculated fields, and API endpoint exposure
    • Workday Web Services (WWS): WSDL reading, SOAP/REST calls, versioning, and error response handling
  • Workday-Native & Functional Fluency:
    • Expert proficiency in XSLT, XML, and JSON; comfortable with Java sufficient for Workday Studio custom steps
    • Working knowledge of the Business Process Framework and how events trigger integration flows
    • Familiarity with Workday functional configuration across HCM, Benefits, Payroll, Security, and Time & Absence, sufficient to independently diagnose upstream data and process issues (deep functional configuration expertise is not required)
    • Foundational understanding of HR and payroll processes and how they generate the data that integrations carry
  • Modern Engineering & AI:
    • REST API design and OAuth 2.0, including user-context (authorization code) flows and token lifecycle handling
    • Experience building or integrating LLM-based tools, AI agents, or MCP servers with enterprise business systems, including permission-safe access patterns and human-in-the-loop controls
    • Experience integrating Workday with middleware or iPaaS platforms (MuleSoft, Boomi, Workato) and the judgment to know when middleware fits versus Workday-native integration
    • Git-based version control and structured deployment and change management practices
  • Security, Compliance & Engineering Practices:
    • Strong knowledge of data security for HR data: OAuth 2.0, SAML, secure file transfer (PGP, SFTP), PII handling, and audit requirements
    • Proven experience managing integrations across Workday’s semi-annual release cycle, including impact assessment and sandbox testing
    • Demonstrated record as a technical leader who has shaped architecture decisions and raised engineering quality across a team
    • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; able to write clear design documents and runbooks, and present technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders
    • Ability to operate effectively in unstructured, fast-moving environments and drive toward outcomes under ambiguity
    • Experience working in an Agile/Scrum environment

Preferred

  • Workday Pro Certification in Integrations (highly valued)
  • Hands-on experience with Workday Extend (data models, UI pages, Extend REST APIs, orchestrations); accelerates ramp into Extend build work
  • Workday Pro Certification in Extend
  • Hands-on experience with Workday Orchestrate
  • Proficiency in TypeScript/Node and Python for services, tooling, and test harnesses outside the Workday tenant
  • Familiarity with Workday’s native agentic capabilities (Agent Ready Tools, MCP Explorer, Workday Agents) and their trade-offs versus custom MCP tooling
  • Experience shipping LLM plugins or agents to an enterprise employee population, including evaluation and quality review
  • Experience supporting global, multi-country HR technology environments
  • Knowledge of GDPR, India DPDP, SOC 2, or SOX requirements in the context of HR data flows
  • SQL and data-warehouse fluency for reconciliation, analytics, and People Analytics partnership

title: Staff Advanced Analytics, Community Blueprint & Quality
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The Quality & Blueprint team sits at the center of how Airbnb understands and improves the customer experience. We partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Finance to identify where the experience is breaking down, why it's breaking down, and what to do about it, so we can keep delighting the Airbnb community at scale. Our work informs strategy at the leadership level and decisions at the product squad level.

The Difference You Will Make:

This role will act as a senior analytics leader on the Community Blueprint Quality team. You'll deliver high-impact analysis, experimentation, and reporting that drives how the business diagnoses and improves the guest and host experience. This is a hands-on, execution-focused role designed to accelerate progress during a period of constrained capacity. You will operate independently, partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders, and own end-to-end work from problem framing to leadership-ready recommendations.

A Typical Day:

  • Conduct strategic deep dives into customer experience drivers (cleanliness, check-in, communication, etc.) to identify symptoms, diagnose root causes, and recommend interventions.
  • Design, execute, and analyze experiments (A/B tests and quasi-experiments) to measure the impact of quality and blueprint initiatives.
  • Build and apply causal inference frameworks (diff-in-diff, synthetic controls, propensity matching) to estimate the true impact of product, policy, and operational changes.
  • Leverage LLMs and AI-assisted analytics to extract structured insights from unstructured data and to scale root-cause taxonomy generation across millions of trips.
  • Develop and validate metrics and dimensions that monitor customer experience health and surface emerging quality issues.
  • Build and maintain analytical artifacts (queries, dashboards, readouts) that let stakeholders self-serve on standard questions.

title: Senior Business Operations and Growth Lead
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

The Chief Business Officer organization drives company-wide growth and global expansion. 

This is the role that turns Airbnb's ambition for the UKI & Nordics into a plan and holds the organisation to delivering it: shaping strategy, aligning cross-functional teams, and driving sustainable commercial growth across one of our most important regions.

This includes recruiting and supporting high-quality Stays, Experiences, and Services, alongside executing Airbnb’s global market strategy. Shaping business approaches, quality supply sourcing, and international growth efforts are integral to the team’s success in connecting millions more hosts and guests to Airbnb's platform.

The Difference You Will Make

You will join the UKI, Nordics, Middle East and Africa team, covering one of Airbnb’s largest and most mature markets alongside five of Europe’s most digitally advanced, high-trust travel markets. The UK offers scale, brand strength, and a sophisticated regulatory environment; the Nordics offer strong domestic travel behaviour and significant headroom for growth. Together they make this one of the most commercially interesting regions in EMEA to build in.

A Typical Day

You will own the business operations agenda for the UKI and Nordics. Airbnb’s most established European market alongside five high-potential Nordic markets (Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland). Partnering closely with the Country Manager, you will set the regional growth strategy, translate it into a plan cross-functional teams can execute against, and run the operating rhythm that keeps it on track. This is a high-visibility role: your influence will come from the quality of your thinking and your ability to mobilise teams to grow further.

Regional growth strategy

  • Own the UKI & Nordics growth strategy end to end: define where the region should compete, what it should stop doing, and the handful of bets that will move guest nights, supply growth, and revenue.
  • Build the annual and quarterly plan with the Country Manager, sizing opportunities and making explicit recommendations on where to deploy marketing spend, supply investment, and partnership effort.
  • Set and pressure-test the region’s targets, translating global goals into market-level commitments that supply, marketing, partnerships, policy, and product teams can own.
  • Run deep-dive analyses on demand and supply dynamics, competitive movements, pricing, and seasonality, turning each into a clear recommendation, not just a read-out.
  • Identify and stand up new growth initiatives, using the UK as a test market for offerings that can then scale across EMEA, and the Nordics as a proving ground for high-penetration, low-friction market plays.
  • Build the case for investment in the region: sizing, business case, and the socialisation needed to win resource in global planning cycles.

Operating rhythm and execution

  • Own the region’s operating cadence: weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews, so leadership has a single, trusted view of performance and the story behind it.
  • Convert strategy into sequenced execution plans with named owners, milestones, and success measures across supply, marketing, partnerships, policy, and product.
  • Track delivery against the plan, surfacing risks and bottlenecks early and driving them to resolution rather than escalating them.
  • Design and continuously improve the operating processes the region runs on, raising the bar on efficiency, transparency, and decision speed.
  • Lead the region’s input into global planning and resource allocation cycles.

Cross-functional leadership

  • Act as the connective tissue between the UKI & Nordics team and global functions such as Product, Marketing, Communications, Policy, Finance, Data Science, Legal, and Community Support.
  • Be the go-to decision partner alongside the Country Manager: the person other teams come to for the region’s position, context, and priorities.
  • Build alignment on high-priority projects, market launches, and product tests, brokering trade-offs between global consistency and local market reality.
  • Represent UKI & Nordics in NEMEA and global business operations forums, and bring the best of what other markets are doing back into the region.
  • Partner with Public Policy on the regulatory landscape, including short-term let rules in the UKI and Nordic city regulation so commercial plans account for policy risk and opportunity.

Insights and storytelling

  • Turn complex data into clear narratives that help leadership decide with a recommendation attached.
  • Build the reporting layer the region relies on: dashboards, performance packs, and executive materials, working with a dedicated analyst.
  • Establish the metrics that matter for the region and hold the team to a shared definition of success.
  • Champion data-driven decision-making, and use AI tooling to compress the time from question to insight. Automating recurring analysis and reporting so the team spends its time on judgement, not assembly.

Your Expertise

To deliver in this role, Airbnb is seeking candidates with:

  • 12+ years in business operations, strategy, consulting, or commercial leadership, with a track record of owning outcomes in a market or business unit
  • Demonstrated ability to set strategy and drive it through to execution 
  • Deep experience influencing without authority across a global matrixed organisation
  • Strong analytical toolkit; comfortable working with finance and data science partners and interrogating the numbers yourself
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, with executive presence in front of senior leadership
  • Comfort with ambiguity, and a strong bias toward action and ownership
  • Practical fluency with AI tools and a view on where they change how a team operates
  • Familiarity with the UKI and/or Nordic markets, or comparable mature-market experience

Additional

  • Experience in a two-sided marketplace, travel/hospitality, or consumer tech
  • Experience launching or scaling new products or lines of business in-market
  • This role will require to be in the London office 3 days per week.

descriptionHtml:

The Community You Will Join

Airbnb is a vision- and mission-driven company. Our Product Managers embody this culture and mindset. They imagine the ideal end state for our community (guests and hosts) and work backward from it, challenging current assumptions. They champion winning strategies, leverage metrics to track progress, and partner with talented cross-functional teammates (engineering, design, data science, and more). Highly hands-on, they are never afraid to roll up their sleeves to deliver the right outcome for our community. If you’re excited to help us create a world where anyone can belong anywhere, we’d love to meet you.

The Difference You Will Make

As a Lead Product Manager for Developer Productivity, you will own the product areas developers rely on, and you will own something harder: the end-to-end workflows that determine how productive our engineers actually are. Those workflows cross organizational boundaries — a single developer journey can touch other parts of the infrastructure, reliability, developer experience, and security. Your job is to understand the end-to-end developer journey, find where it breaks, and drive the work to fix it whether or not the fix lives in your teams.

You will define what developer productivity means at Airbnb, instrument it, and be accountable for moving it. In collaboration with business stakeholders, product marketing, and technical program managers, you will help shape the roadmap for these products, with an emphasis on bringing together disparate offerings into a cohesive infrastructure roadmap.This will include the creation and ownership of Product Requirements Documents (PRDs) and Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) to inform technical decisions. You will also partner with engineers, designers, data scientists, and field-operations teams to scale our solutions across existing and emerging business segments, ensuring a cohesive system view.

  • Own cross-cutting developer workflows end to end — mapping where they break across pillars like App & Cloud Infra, Reliability Engineering, and Developer Experience, and driving the changes that improve them
  • Define how we measure developer productivity: build the metrics, instrumentation, and qualitative research that tell us whether engineers' lives are actually getting better
  • Partner with Engineering, Product, TPM, and Data Science to understand goals and establish success criteria with clearly measurable objectives and key results
  • Develop the product roadmap, and get alignment on prioritization and timelines to meet business goals
  • Influence teams you don't own — build the case, bring the data, and get other groups to prioritize developer productivity work alongside their own roadmaps
  • Develop a deep understanding of how Airbnb's engineers work day to day, and of the technical architecture underneath, to build and improve products that fit into real workflows rather than around them
  • Execute efficiently to ship products and deliver impact for our business and users.
  • Lead cross-functional groups to fulfill the team’s mission, acting as the system voice.
  • Communicate concisely and influence outcomes at all levels of the organization, demonstrating strong executive presence.

Your Expertise

  • 10+ years of product management experience building tools and platforms for technical users — developer tooling, infrastructure, or platform products
  • Track record of improving developer or engineering productivity, with the measurements to prove it
  • Experience defining and operationalizing metrics for hard-to-quantify outcomes — when quantitative metrics are needed and matter, and when qualitative metrics may or may not be more impactful 
  • Strong understanding of technical architecture for complex and highly scalable systems, and of modern AI-powered developer workflows: AI-assisted development, code review, CI/CD, build systems, testing, deployment
  • Demonstrated ability to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries without direct authority — influencing roadmaps you don't own
  • Ability to understand immediate and longer-term customer goals and needs, and build products that meet them
  • Entrepreneurial drive, and demonstrated ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams to align on a vision and product strategy
  • Ability to quickly absorb technical concepts and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical partners at every level of the organization
  • Ability to prioritize and scope user requests and platform capabilities, balancing long-term vision against short-term pain points
  • Previous experience as a software engineer, or working extremely closely with engineering teams, is a strong plus
  • Familiarity with developer productivity research and frameworks (DORA, SPACE, DevEx) is a plus

The Difference You Will Make:

title: Senior Staff Data Engineer, Foundational Data
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

At Airbnb, our mission is to create a world where anyone can belong anywhere. The Foundational Data team builds and operates the high-quality, widely reused datasets that power critical decisions across Airbnb: how visitors are measured from site traffic, how bot traffic is separated from organic traffic, and how cloud costs are attributed to Airbnb services. Our cost dashboards are among the most-used at Airbnb, relied on by technical leads, finance, and executives. Every dollar Airbnb spends running its infrastructure is attributed by models this team owns.

We are now building a third pillar, and it puts this team at the forefront of how Airbnb measures AI: the cost, usage, and performance of the models we train and serve ourselves, and of the AI tools our own engineers use every day. When Airbnb asks whether an AI investment is paying off, the answer comes from datasets this team builds.

Foundational Data sits inside Cloud Infrastructure and is a deliberate mix of Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers working as one team.

The Difference You Will Make:

As a Senior Staff Data Engineer, you are the technical leader for this team and the person who sets its direction. This is a hands-on role with no direct reports: you will own the long-term data architecture and you will build against it, from the Airflow-orchestrated pipelines that ingest telemetry, logs, and billing data through to the dimensional models and Minerva definitions that thousands of people at Airbnb reason with. Because we are a mixed DE and AE team, you will work across both disciplines: this role needs data engineering depth, plus enough fluency in metric and dimensional modeling to set direction for the analytics engineering side.

Infrastructure intelligence is where you will start, and it is fresh ground. The signals describing our fleets are fragmented across cost, utilization telemetry, service performance, and GPU and model telemetry. Nobody has modeled this coherently yet, and the AI side is the least charted part of all. There is no schema to inherit. You would decide what these datasets are, then bring the rest of the company along.

This work carries regular visibility to directors and VPs across Infrastructure and Finance.

A Typical Day:

  • Provide technical leadership across the team's data engineering and analytics engineering work, spanning cloud cost, traffic & bots, and infrastructure intelligence
  • Define and own the multi-year data strategy and architecture for Airbnb's foundational data assets, and build the cross-org consensus needed to fund and execute it
  • Own how Airbnb measures its AI: the unit economics of training and serving our own models, GPU fleet utilization, and the cost and adoption of developer AI tooling
  • Design and build the datasets that integrate cost, utilization, performance, and reliability signals across Airbnb's infrastructure fleets, starting from a blank page
  • Stay hands-on in the pipelines and models you architect, close enough to the build to catch the problems design reviews miss
  • Influence and coach a distributed team of Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers, raising the quality bar through design and code review and scaling it by building the frameworks and automated checks other teams adopt
  • Navigate conflicting stakeholder requirements across Infrastructure, Finance, Data Science, and Product Engineering, and land a single definition everyone can build on
  • Identify and eliminate duplication and data fragmentation across the engineering organization, driving deprecation of what your models replace
  • Participate in the team's on-call rotation for the datasets we own

Your Expertise:

You do not need prior experience with cloud cost, infrastructure, or AI/ML data to succeed here. What we cannot teach is the following.

  • 12+ years of relevant industry experience with a BS/Masters, or 9+ years with a PhD, in data engineering or a closely related field
  • You have designed, built, and operated production data pipelines at large scale, and you write strong SQL and Python. Scala experience is useful but not required
  • You can design a dimensional model and define a metric others will trust, even if analytics engineering has not been your job title
  • You have moved into an unfamiliar data or technical domain and become productive quickly, building enough understanding of the underlying systems to model them well
  • You have been the technical lead on a team or program, setting direction that other senior engineers executed against without formal authority over them, while still writing code yourself
  • You have written the multi-year technical strategy for an area, and got other organizations to fund and deliver against it
  • You have built a data product where no schema or precedent existed, and persuaded other teams to adopt it
  • You have written the document that aligned several teams on a contested technical decision, and you can explain a data model to a finance partner as readily as to an engineer

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Trust
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

Everyone at Airbnb thinks about trust, but our team obsesses over it daily. At the core of trust is safety, and thus we spend a significant amount of our time and energy keeping the community safe. The Trust team is responsible for developing the technology that helps protect our community and platform from fraud while also ensuring our hosts, guests, homes, and experiences meet our high standards. We constantly work to fight against online fraud (such as monetary loss, compromised accounts, spam and scam in messages, fake inventory, etc.) as well as offline fraud (theft, property damage, personal safety, etc.). We also work on onboarding and screening of users, and think about complex topics like identity and reputation to ensure that every interaction with Airbnb helps build trust in us and our community.

You'll work side-by-side with talented product managers, data scientists, software engineers, fraud intelligence, and operations teams. Together, you'll design and build ML solutions that have direct, meaningful impact on user trust, business success, and the global Airbnb community.

The Difference You Will Make:

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Trust team, you will actively contribute code and ideas that shape the ML systems protecting millions of Airbnb users. You'll own and deliver ML projects end-to-end — from designing and training models to productionizing and operating them at scale, while collaborating closely with cross-functional partners.

You'll tackle real-world challenges such as account takeover, fake accounts, payment fraud, and bot detection. Your work will help reduce risks posed by bad actors while ensuring the platform remains seamless and welcoming for everyone else. As you develop your skills, you'll see the tangible impact of your models, helping real users stay safe and confident as they travel, host, and connect on Airbnb.

A Typical Day: 

  • Collaborate with product managers, data scientists, software engineers, and operations teams to identify opportunities, scope ML solutions, and refine requirements for new or improved Trust models.
  • Design, build, and productionize end-to-end Machine Learning pipelines, including feature engineering, model training, evaluation, and deployment — for both batch and real-time use cases.
  • Investigate emerging fraud patterns and threat signals with your teammates, and develop ML-based detections and tools that enable faster, more accurate responses.
  • Write, review, and ship clean, testable code — whether training a new model, improving an existing pipeline, or optimizing a feature for scalability and reliability.
  • Work with large-scale structured and unstructured data to continuously improve ML models for Airbnb product, business, and operational use cases.
  • Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and cross-team collaborations to contribute to a high-quality ML engineering culture.
  • Work closely with trust defense and platform teams to adapt models and systems to an evolving landscape of fraud attacks.
  • Build and optimize top-of-funnel fraud detection models to improve early detection and strengthen system-wide fraud defenses.
  • Explore, prototype, and productionize innovative ML models and techniques to detect and counter emerging fraud vectors.
  • Explore and leverage LLMs and GenAI technologies to advance fraud and abuse detection, investigation, and response capabilities.

Your Expertise:

  • 5+ years of industry experience in applied Machine Learning, with a track record of building and productionizing models at scale.
  • Strong programming skills in Python (required) and familiarity with Scala, Java, or equivalent.
  • Solid understanding of Machine Learning best practices — e.g., training/serving skew minimization, A/B testing, feature engineering, model selection — and algorithms such as gradient boosted trees, neural networks, transformers, and deep learning.
  • Experience with ML frameworks and tooling such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, or equivalent.
  • Experience with data engineering and building end-to-end ML pipelines, including both batch and real-time systems.
  • Exposure to architectural patterns of large, high-scale software applications (e.g., well-designed APIs, high-volume data pipelines, efficient algorithms).
  • Experience with test-driven development, incremental delivery, and deployment practices.
  • Exposure to the Trust and Risk domain (e.g., fraud detection, anomaly detection, identity, account integrity) is a plus.
  • A Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in CS/ML or a related field.
  • Experience designing and implementing ML evaluation frameworks, including ground truth, offline and online metrics, and model calibration.
  • Experience with or strong interest in LLMs and GenAI technologies is a plus.

descriptionHtml:

The Community and Product Policy team creates and evolves principled policies that establish the rules of the road for guests and hosts across Airbnb. We solve complex marketplace and Trust & Safety challenges using data, stakeholder collaboration, and excellent judgement to support our community at scale. We team up with our cross-functional partners to create clear and accessible policy enforcement guides and to continuously measure, maintain, and improve our policies. We handle policy escalations and consults from across the business to ensure tough calls are resolved in accordance with our principles.

The Difference You Will Make

  • You are a seasoned policy expert, with experience handling complex escalations
  • You love solving problems and have a track record of strong cross-functional collaboration
  • You’re an experienced communicator, with exceptional writing skills and presentation skills, including to senior executive audiences
  • You are principled and rigorous — you incorporate diverse perspectives in pursuit of the best decisions and outcomes possible
  • You are fluent with AI tools for gaining operational efficiency, but you exercise excellent judgement and know human expertise and supervision is paramount
  • You can build and interrogate prompting, automated workflows, data queries, and stress-test model output before it reaches a decision-maker — you know when a number is not trustworthy and how to course correct
  • You are a team player who thrives in a fast-moving environment and brings a strategic mindset to your work 

As a Consults and Escalations Manager in Community Policy, you will work across the business to understand every aspect of a case. You’ll provide timely policy analysis and corresponding enforcement recommendations, and continuously evaluate and improve our policies to handle new issues as they arise. You will resolve individual user matters and translate what you learn into policy insights and recommended changes — using your case handling expertise alongside AI and data tooling you will detect patterns across escalation volume. You'll automate things like detection and reporting, but you'll make the judgment call, document the reasoning, and own the outcome. You will help our leaders understand recurring issues and how we can fix them in the future. This role will serve as an important player in developing our global policy improvements and will have a direct impact on the peace of mind of millions of Airbnb community members around the world.

A Typical Day

  • Drive complicated escalations and issues towards a solution
  • Advise our operations teams on cases where there are policy gaps to arrive at a solution that is guided by Airbnb’s principles and values
  • Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders across the business including but not limited to the Global Operations, Supply, Public Policy, Legal, Product, Trust and Safety, Communications and Partnerships
  • Build AI-assisted detection of repeat policy questions and gray areas, turning consult volume into a standing signal to help drive trainings and policy clarifications
  • Query, join, and visualize operational data to evaluate policy performance and pressure-test policy improvement recommendations before they reach leadership
  • Design and ship workflows that reduce avoidable consults, cut handling time on the rest, and measure the gain
  • Exercise final judgment on ambiguous, high-exposure escalations, and make the reasoning exceptionally clear to Legal, Ops, and executives

Your Expertise

  • 6+ years experience in an Operations, Policy, Legal, or Trust and Safety role
  • A track record of strong leadership in handling issues and escalations
  • Demonstrated capacity for critical thinking, research, and analysis; strong attention to detail
  • Exceptional writing and presentation abilities to explain and simplify complex information to others
  • Thoughtful business judgment, strategic thinking, and ability to work well under pressure
  • Experience working in a matrix and driving solutions to complex problems through cross-functional collaboration
  • Fluency in data analysis and demonstrated use of AI tools to create operational leverage — with the discipline to validate any output and the judgment to know what should not be delegated to a model

Preferred Experience

  • Experience working closely with operations teams, preferably in the Trust and Safety space
  • Experience building or piloting AI/LLM-assisted workflows in operations, policy, or compliance
  • Familiarity with quality measurement or QA frameworks for frontline teams

descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

UX Writing is a core design discipline at Airbnb. Our team of 40+ writers works closely with Experience Design, Experience Research, Engineering, and Design Program Management to support the product development process from beginning to end. Whether you excel in upfront storytelling, end-to-end systems design, or nitty-gritty execution, you'll find your people here.

The Difference You Will Make:

From concept to launch, our UX writers create industry-leading experiences for guests and hosts that meaningfully impact the success of the company. In this role, you'll shape how AI-powered, generative surfaces speak to hosts and you'll build the systems that keep that voice consistent as models change. You'll help set the standard for how our team partners with Engineering to define the ideal experience, evaluate generated output, and iterate to improve the product, and you'll bring the rest of UX Writing along with you.

A Typical Day:

  • Lead all work related to the words across multiple projects within a single initiative—this includes both creating clear, concise, and delightful copy for your product surface yourself on some surfaces, and training large language models that ultimately create the copy on others 
  • Develop inspiring, strategic ideas based on product requirements, data, and/or research
  • Set the quality bar for AI-generated content: write the guidelines and examples, grade and rank model outputs, and calibrate VJs 
  • Drive consensus with stakeholders and/or partners on content recommendations
  • Manage copy deadlines and deliver detailed copy across multiple projects
  • Connect with our critical cross-functional partners including Design, PM, Legal, accessibility, and localization to ensure we have the proper input on our work
  • Join writing team crits to present work and help sharpen the work of your teammates
  • Present content and design work to directors, executives, or other stakeholders on your projects
  • Set the bar on every surface with judgment and taste

Your Expertise:

  • 10+ years of experience in UX writing, content design, or content strategy
  • Proven ability to lead content/copy work from concept to detailed design
  • Experience in LLM prompting, generative AI, and model evaluation, with a point of view on training writing quality into a model
  • Proven systems thinking and product strategy 
  • Experience building systems—guidelines, reference examples, evals—that scale across a team
  • Experience writing content principles, messaging frameworks, and style guides, and adapting them into guidelines a model can be trained and evaluated against
  • Proven ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams in all stages of design and build
  • Proven ability to lead systems work from concept to detailed design, including defining net-new process where none exists
  • Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with the flexibility to adjust course as models and priorities shift
  • Familiar working alongside other design disciplines in Figma, our primary collaboration tool
  • Experience working with and presenting to executive teams
  • Solid understanding of user experience design principles and interaction patterns
  • Passion for Airbnb's mission, commitment to diversity, and global mindset

Your Location:

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager and will lean toward PST hours. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. title: Senior Demand Generation Specialist, Hotels (12M FTC)
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The Airbnb Hotels organization is a fun, entrepreneurial, start-up team where you can have outsized impact. Simplicity is at the core of our products. We pride ourselves on delivering the smoothest and most intuitive hotel booking experience. For hotels, we make it easy to drive incremental bookings so they can focus on the craft of hosting. We aspire to facilitate hotel discovery and serendipity at scale, benefitting guests and hotel partners.

The Difference You will Make:

Airbnb is building the world's largest supply of boutique and independent hotels on its platform. To accelerate that growth, we're hiring a Senior Demand Generation Specialist to own the inbound engine for our Hotels Acquisition team.

This is a high-impact, strategic and hands-on role sitting at the intersection of marketing and sales. This is Airbnb's first-ever B2B demand generation role. You'll build the Hotels inbound motion from the ground up across EMEA, as a 12-month pilot that will shape how we scale it globally.

This role is remote within France or Italy. We are not able to support relocation for this role.

A Typical Day: 

  • Define and own the EMEA inbound strategy and roadmap, prioritising the channels and initiatives that will drive the most hotel go-lives
  • Build and scale multi-channel inbound programs (email, paid, SEO, content, events, partnerships) targeting independent hotels, boutique chains, and hotel groups globally
  • Own the full funnel from lead capture to MQL handoff, including lead scoring, routing, and CRM hygiene in Salesforce, in collaboration with RevOps Teams
  • Design Linkedin campaigns in coordination with regional AE teams to target high-priority segments and geographies
  • Develop outbound-assist sequences (via tools like Mixmax or Outreach) to complement AE prospecting
  • Partner with Global Marketing to build collateral, landing pages, and nurture flows that speak to hotel operator pain points
  • Track, report, and optimize against pipeline contribution metrics: MQLs, MQL-to-SQL conversion, cost per lead, and influenced revenue
  • Run co-marketing and referral programs with industry partners (channel managers, PMSes, hospitality associations)
  • Build business cases for each campaign, secure budget from stakeholders, and show clear ROI
  • Run a test-and-learn approach: launch quickly, measure, cut what doesn't work and scale what does
  • Use AI and automation to scale campaign creation, content and lead nurture
  • Work with Connectivity, Events, Country Managers and AEs to turn webinars, events and partnerships into measurable pipeline

Your Expertise:

  • 8+ years of experience in B2B demand generation or growth marketing, ideally within marketplace, hospitality tech, or SaaS environments
  • Proven track record of building inbound programs that generate measurable sales pipeline, including experience building a demand gen function from scratch (startup, scale-up, or new-business environment)
  • Hands-on experience with Salesforce, marketing automation tools (MixMax, Outreach, or similar), and paid channels
  • Strong analytical, systems-driven approach; comfortable running campaigns yourself, not just briefing others
  • Data-driven: you own your funnel metrics and can connect campaign activity to revenue impact
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools to automate campaigns and create content at scale
  • Strong sales alignment instincts; you treat AEs as internal customers
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: able to shape your own scope, make the case for investment, and adjust quickly based on results
  • Fluent in written and spoken English; additional European languages a plus
  • Experience operating globally across multiple regions/languages a plus

Why This Role:

Airbnb Hotels is one of the company's highest-priority supply growth initiatives. This role sits at the center of that effort, with direct visibility to senior leadership and the ability to shape how the world's most recognized travel brand expands into professional hospitality. 

As the first person in this role, you'll help show what B2B demand generation can do for Airbnb Hotels. While this is a 12-month fixed-term contract, a successful pilot could lead to the role continuing beyond the initial term.

title: Senior Social Manager, Instagram
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

At Airbnb, Instagram is where our brand shows up most visibly. It’s where travel, culture, and belonging come to life - not as a point of sale, but as something people choose to spend time with. This role will help define that presence, shaping a feed that feels considered, culturally fluent, and distinctly Airbnb.

We’re looking for someone who can combine creative instinct, editorial judgment, and platform expertise to build something innovative and enduring. Someone excited by setting the tone, raising the bar, and defining what great looks like - while still moving at the speed of culture.

The Difference You Will Make

We’re looking for someone who understands Instagram at a deep, almost instinctive level - not just how it works, but how to win at it. 

You probably spend more time on the platform than anyone you know. You see patterns before they become trends, understand the signals behind the algorithm, and have a clear point of view on what makes content travel - and what makes it feel stale.

More than anything, you think like an editor. You have a vision and can articulate taste. You know what’s worth saying, how to say it, and when. You understand pacing, sequencing, and how individual posts ladder up into a broader narrative.

You’ve likely played a meaningful role in shaping and growing an account, with a strong perspective on format, visual language, and storytelling. You understand the nuances of Reels, Carousels, Stories  - and how each can be used to build a cohesive, evolving point of view for Airbnb

A Typical Day:

  • Air traffic control all content across social media to ensure everything works coherently together. 
  • Ideate, conceptualise, and create Instagram-native content for Airbnb's owned channel across Reels, Carousels, and Stories
  • Partner closely with internal teams and external creators to develop original content designed specifically for the platform
  • Maintain a deep and constantly evolving understanding of Instagram trends, formats, algorithm dynamics, and audience behavior
  • Develop original, repeatable content frameworks that move beyond trend participation and build a coherent, evolving brand narrative
  • Own accurate, timely publishing and real-time community engagement on Instagram
  • Partner with analytics teams to measure impact, extract insights, and continuously refine strategy and creative output

Your Expertise:

  • Have managed or significantly grown an Instagram account - for a brand, creator, or yourself
  • Bring a strong editorial point of view and a clear sense of taste across content, design, and storytelling
  • Understand how content performs on Instagram - and can articulate why and be the voice to influence how we show up on the platform
  • Can move from idea to execution seamlessly - concepting, articulating and publishing social-native content
  • Think in ideas and community, not just posts - shaping how content connects with audiences over time
  • Can dive in with community development and management in a way that feels ownable and distinctive for our brand 
  • Spot cultural moments early and translate them into relevant, on-brand storytelling
  • Are constantly pushing for work that feels sharper, more distinctive, and more culturally resonant
  • Thrive in fast-moving environments and are comfortable making decisions with imperfect information

title: Senior Software Engineer, Streaming Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

Airbnb's Data Infrastructure organization builds the systems that store, move, and transform data across the company. Our Data Movement & Transformation (DMT) group is building a single, unified platform for moving data between Airbnb's storage systems, replacing dozens of one-off tools with one reliable, well-supported way to get data where it needs to go. This platform is the foundation for Data as a Service, a top-level infrastructure initiative at Airbnb.

The Community You Will Join:

The Ingestion team is the front door to DMT. We build and operate two managed, multi-tenant platforms that move data out of Airbnb's online databases for offline processing:

  • SpinalTap: near real-time change data capture (CDC) streaming to Kafka for every Aurora and UDS table at Airbnb.
  • DBExports: periodic full-table snapshots and mutation exports.

Teams across Airbnb depend on these systems, including payments, fraud detection, financial reporting, search, messaging, notifications, and machine learning. Reliability, performance, and scale are the product. You'll work closely with DMT's other teams, which own real-time streaming infrastructure, pipeline orchestration, and schema management, and you'll have the chance to work across the broader platform

The Difference You Will Make:

  • Be hands-on (code, design, test) and work with partner teams, internal customers, and leadership to deliver multi-month projects on time.
  • Design, build, and operate large-scale CDC and batch export systems that run across every online database at Airbnb.
  • Help shape the architecture of DMT's unified data movement platform while it's being built.
  • Improve the reliability, performance, and efficiency of systems that critical business functions depend on.
  • Make it easier for engineers at Airbnb to get their data into offline systems without needing to be database or pipeline experts.
  • Take part in on-call and raise the operational bar for a platform that other teams build on.

Your Expertise:

  • 5+ years of experience building and operating large-scale backend distributed systems, such as data ingestion, streaming, CDC, storage, or data platforms.
  • Hands-on experience with streaming systems like Kafka, and with how databases capture and publish changes (binlogs, Debezium, or similar).
  • Ability to own and go deep in a complex codebase.
  • Experience maintaining, analyzing, and debugging production systems at scale.
  • Clean, readable, testable, and maintainable code.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in a remote-working environment.
  • Strong ownership and a track record of delivering on time.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience building managed or multi-tenant platforms used by other engineering teams.
  • Familiarity with MySQL/Aurora, schema evolution, or large-scale batch data processing.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Data Authoring
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community you will join

Airbnb's Data Authoring Platform exists to turn raw data into decision-grade insight, fast, reliable, and at scale. We provide a single, paved path for 4,000+ internal data producers and consumers to model, transform, and serve trustworthy data and metrics that power everything from A/B experimentation to executive dashboards.

What we own:

  • Minerva, Airbnb's semantic layer & metrics platform, ensuring one definition of truth across the company.
  • The end-to-end data-authoring framework that cuts through pipeline boilerplate and accelerates iteration, pipeline testing, and validation.
  • Tooling for reliability, governance, and cost-efficiency, including automated testing, anomaly detection, and right-sized materialization.

The difference you will make

As a Staff Software Engineer focused on Minerva, you will own and drive high-impact workstreams end to end. You'll take ambiguous problem spaces, such as making experimentation faster and easier, talk to users, define the work, and deliver it. Your work will help thousands of internal users define, understand, and consume trustworthy business metrics across product, finance, BI, and experimentation.

Engineers, designers, and product leaders rely on these tools to explore and develop new product experiences and to run experiments that tell them what is right for our customers. Depending on your background, you may partner closely with the experimentation team to find gaps and shape how Minerva serves them.

We believe data is the voice of our customers at scale. The tools you build will help improve the Airbnb product for every guest and host.

A typical day

  • Build and extend Minerva's core services, including our query rewriting service.
  • Take on loosely defined problems, partner with users and teams to scope them, and propose and deliver solutions.
  • Track semantic layer techniques and database engine capabilities to inform priorities.
  • Partner with teams across the company to make data easier to query and use.
  • Own design, implementation, testing, and on-call for the systems you build.

Your expertise

  • 9+ years of hands-on software engineering, with the majority of your time spent building and deploying production applications and services (rather than writing configuration and SQL).
  • Deep proficiency in at least one modern general-purpose language (e.g., Java, Kotlin, Scala, Go, Python, TypeScript).
  • Experience working on data platforms or data tooling, with a good understanding of why users want to do what they do with data. Prior data engineering or data science experience is a plus, but software engineering should be your primary focus.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently scope and drive ambiguous, cross-team projects from design through launch.
  • Strong command of OOP, API design, and distributed systems patterns.
  • Strong communication skills and experience working across complex team and system interfaces.

Nice to haves

  • Experience with experimentation platforms (assignment, metrics, analysis, or experiment tooling).
  • Experience with metrics, semantic layer, BI, or analytics platforms (e.g., dbt, Tableau, Superset).
  • Experience with query engines, query rewriting/optimization, or data warehouse internals.
  • Experience authoring DSLs, compilers, or APIs that abstract data transformations.

title: Business Operations and Growth Lead, Asia
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community you will join:

The Chief Business Officer (CBO) organization drives Airbnb's growth and expansion around the world, commercializing our new and existing businesses and executing our global strategy in the market. The Global Markets team sits within CBO and makes sure Airbnb is locally relevant everywhere we operate, working with regions to plan and execute growth across supply, demand, and the surfaces our communities use.

Asia is one of the largest growth opportunities in that portfolio and one of the most complex regions to run: Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia sit at very different stages of maturity, with distinct competitive sets, regulatory contexts and consumer behaviour. Over the past year, the region has built a new operating system and scaled multiple growth levers from single-market pilots to regional programs. That growth has outpaced our capacity to run it: business reporting, program delivery and the cross-functional roadmap currently sit with one person alongside the regional strategy agenda. We are building a dedicated capability to own how Asia operates and how Asia delivers, and we want you at the centre of it.

The difference you will make:

This role is based in Singapore and requires regular travel across Asia.

In this role you report to the Senior Business Operations and Growth Lead, Asia and work closely with country Business Operations and Growth Leads across Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia, alongside central teams in growth marketing, product, payments, supply, policy and brand. You own the Asia business reporting and operating cadence, and you lead the delivery of the region's growth levers and its cross-functional roadmap.

This is deliberately an ownership role in insights and execution, distinct from the roles around it. Countries own their market plans and outcomes, growth marketing, product and merchandising teams build the platforms, and Strategic Finance and Advanced Analytics own objective tracking and measurement standards. You own the connective tissue between them: the reporting that gives the region one accurate and current picture, the delivery of growth levers into market, the roadmap accountability that keeps cross-functional commitments on track, and the competitive read that tells us where we are gaining and losing.

A typical day:

  • Lead the end-to-end operations and delivery of selected regional growth levers including go-to-market, measurement and optimization
  • Own the regional business reporting structure, inputs and cadence regionally and globally
  • Own the regional view of the cross-functional roadmap across supply, product, payments, policy, brand and growth marketing, and drive accountability on delivery through cross-functional collaboration

title: Senior Manager, Vendor Operations & Customer Support
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

Every year, millions of guests and Hosts across EMEA and LATAM reach out to us at moments that matter, a booking that fell through, a stay that didn't go to plan, a question that needs a clear answer in their own language. How we show up in those moments decides whether they come back.

We're looking for a senior operations leader to own that outcome. You'll lead a network of outsourced BPO partners delivering customer support across one of Airbnb's most complex regions, and you'll be accountable for the quality our community actually experiences, measured above all by NPS.

This is a performance leadership role, not an administrative one. You'll build the frameworks, insight loops and performance culture that genuinely move partner performance, and you'll lead a team of Partner Operations Managers who make that happen across every language, market and site.

What we're looking for:

  • Deep experience managing outsourced BPO partners and vendor relationships across multiple locations, ideally spanning EMEA, LATAM or another complex multi-region remit
  • A proven track record of improving customer experience metrics at scale (NPS or CSAT), not just reporting on them
  • Strong people leadership, including leading managers or senior individual contributors
  • Comfort operating across multiple markets and languages in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment
  • Experience leading through operational incidents or crises, knowing who to pull in across the business and how to drive resolution
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration, working closely with internal teams such as Workforce Management, Quality, and Country & Business Operations to land changes that improve outcomes

What you'll do

Lead vendor delivery and performance

  • Own end-to-end customer support delivery across a network of outsourced partners in EMEA and LATAM, spanning multiple channels, languages and service tiers
  • Hold partners accountable to committed performance across NPS, quality, resolution, service level, efficiency and cost,  including the difficult conversations when results fall short
  • Set clear, outcomes-driven performance frameworks and a standardised operating playbook so delivery is consistent across every site and market
  • Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with partner leadership and Airbnb senior leadership, moving the conversation from reporting to committed, dated actions and updates on progress across key initiatives and objectives
  • Build relationships with leaders across the business and use them to unlock performance rather than to manage escalations
  • Understand all the contributing factors of performance and make deliberate trade-offs between quality, capacity and cost

Raise the bar on NPS through insight

  • Diagnose what is genuinely driving performance gaps, market, language, tier, partner, agent tenure, contact driver, policy or product and separate signal from noise
  • Turn that diagnosis into robust, clear, time-bound improvement plans with named owners, and drive them to a measurable NPS outcome
  • Bring the voice of the customer upstream: where the root cause sits in policy, product or process, make the case for the fix with evidence
  • Test, scale and retire performance interventions with discipline, so what works becomes standard and what doesn't is stopped quickly

Grow a strong team

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of Partner Operation Managers, building deep capability in performance diagnosis, partner influence and data fluency
  • Set clear expectations and a high bar, give direct and useful feedback, and create real development paths for your team
  • Build a team culture that is inclusive, curious and resilient, working effectively across many cultures, languages and time zones
  • Grow your own successors , make the team stronger than you found it

Collaborate to make performance consistent

  • Work across regions and shared services within Community Support so strong performance is designed in globally, not rebuilt locally
  • Partner with Workforce Management, Quality, Learning & Development, to land the operational changes that improve customer outcomes
  • Support the rollout and adoption of strategic customer experience initiatives, and be a clear voice for what will and won't work in market
  • Adopt and share external best practice in partner performance management

Drive trust and repeat business at market level

  • Partner with the Country & Business Operations (CBO) teams on cross-functional, market-specific initiatives that build trust and drive repeat business
  • Translate market-level commercial and community priorities into support delivery decisions and translate support insight back into market strategy
  • Bring local nuance into a global operating model: what earns trust in one market is not what earns trust in another, and the plan should reflect that

What success looks like

Headline metric: NPS across EMEA and LATAM supported languages, at or ahead of target.

Supporting outcomes:

  • Quality, resolution and service level performance consistently meeting commitments across every partner site
  • Every performance gap has a clear, evidenced root cause and a live plan with a named owner and a date
  • Efficiency and cost-per-contact managed within plan, without trading away customer experience
  • A standardised operating playbook adopted across the partner network, with measurably less variance between sites
  • A high-performing, engaged POM team with strong internal mobility
  • Strong operational execution plans for peak travel periods
  • Market-level trust and repeat-business initiatives delivered with CBO, with measurable impact

What you'll bring

Required

  • 10+ years' experience in customer support, service delivery or partner/BPO operations, including significant time at senior level
  • Proven track record of owning and improving customer experience metrics at scale, ideally NPS or CSAT
  • Substantial experience managing outsourced partners or vendors, including performance management accountability and QBR ownership
  • Experience leading and developing managers or senior individual contributors
  • Strong analytical capability — comfortable interrogating data yourself, not only consuming a dashboard
  • Experience operating in a global, matrixed, multicultural organisation
  • Degree in business or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Preferred

  • Experience across both EMEA and LATAM, or another multi-region remit
  • Onshore and offshore delivery experience
  • Additional language relevant to the region (Spanish, Portuguese, French, German or Italian)
  • Experience in a marketplace, travel or two-sided platform business
  • Familiarity with AI and automation in customer support and how to deploy it without eroding trust

descriptionHtml:
