title: Campaign Manager, Mexico
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

Airbnb's Public Policy team works closely with federal, state and municipal governments, legislators, regulators, public entities, industry associations, academia, our host community and the broader public. We introduce them to Airbnb, highlight the social and economic contribution our community makes to Mexico and its local communities, and share best practices from around the world.

Our goal is twofold. We want policymakers to understand the regulatory challenges that affect our hosts and to find models that work for cities, towns and their residents. We also want to help Mexican society embrace an innovative, collaborative economy where everyone can belong.

As part of a wider regional policy team, we take part in many local, state and national conversations at once. We engage governments directly and involve our community and partners in making the case for fair, progressive home sharing rules. Our work is organized in local campaign pods that draw on a wide range of tools: detailed policy analysis, strategic partnerships, policy media, community organizing, digital tactics, polling, data science and research, and persuasive policy narratives.

The Difference You will Make:

The Public Policy Campaign Manager leads the design and execution of successful policy campaigns in Mexico, working with the Public Policy Lead on both daily operations and overall strategy. You will draft and run integrated engagement plans, using in-person and digital tools to move key stakeholders toward specific policy goals in response to active or developing legislation and regulation.

A central part of the role is building trust with local authorities. You will help them understand the contribution our community makes, and engage them in creating fair legal and regulatory frameworks that embrace the potential of the sharing economy.

You are meticulously organized, detail-oriented and focused on solutions. You see the big picture, prioritize strategically, and know which information and data to escalate to leadership. You turn big ideas into policy with a positive, creative outlook, and you build strong relationships with internal teams and stakeholders in Mexico, the region and globally.

A Typical Day: 

  • Develop and implement Airbnb's legislative and public policy activities in Mexico, including advocacy priorities, positions and strategies.
  • Review legislative and regulatory language, draft comments and research issues to provide analysis on proposals affecting Airbnb's priorities.
  • Build and represent Airbnb in coalitions and collaborations that advance our advocacy goals, creating them from scratch when needed.
  • Maintain relationships with an extensive network of contacts in local, state and national legislative, executive and administrative offices, as well as allied groups and coalition partners.
  • Represent Airbnb in meetings with government and elected officials, industry associations, Airbnb hosts and other stakeholders.
  • Represent Airbnb at public speaking engagements as directed by the Public Policy Lead for Mexico & CCA.
  • Recruit and manage consultants and agencies, and marshal external resources to execute campaign plans.
  • Advise Airbnb teams on public policy matters to guide the development of products, services and policies.
  • Work closely with local business partners so that campaign plans fit with business priorities and outcomes.
  • Monitor and track legislation and regulatory matters, and advise the company on policy challenges.
  • Report progress accurately and regularly, and flag roadblocks in a timely way.

Your Expertise:

  • At least 10 years of experience in public policy, direct lobbying or government relations in a business, political, governmental, legislative or regulatory context, such as tourism and accommodation, e-commerce and platform regulation, housing and landlord/tenant law, or tax.
  • Proven experience managing complex regulatory and political issues, whether in-house, as a consultant, or in politics, campaigns or advocacy groups.
  • Proficiency in regulatory and legislative drafting.
  • Ability to quickly get up to speed on complex technical and regulatory issues.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex projects at once and navigate a matrix organization with many stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, including planning, memo-writing and basic budgeting.
  • Creative and entrepreneurial, with a proven track record of being proactive and results-driven without sacrificing quality.
  • Excellent communicator with strong presentation, writing and interpersonal skills.
  • Full fluency in Spanish and English, reading, writing and speaking.
  • Acute attention to detail; extremely organized and able to help keep others organized.
  • Sound judgment and the ability to maintain confidentiality.
  • Poised under pressure, flexible, and positive about change and challenges.
  • Able to work independently and as a team player, with a sense of humor and the ability to thrive in a fast-moving, sometimes stressful environment.
  • Passion for Airbnb, home sharing and the collaborative economy.

title: Senior Manager, Community Policy
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join: 

In Community Policy, our mission is to create and evolve principled policies that establish the rules of the road for guests and hosts across Airbnb. This involves solving some of the most complex Trust & Safety challenges of our time. Our work is informed by rigorous research and stakeholder collaboration, and we design policies that can support our community at scale. We team with our cross-functional partners to create accessible policy enforcement guides and to continuously maintain and improve our policies.

The Difference You Will Make:

As a Senior Manager for Community Policy, you will partner closely with stakeholders across the company to support Airbnb's strategic objectives. You will lead policy development in the anti-discrimination and safety space, addressing real-world harms and ensuring every host and guest is treated fairly. This role entails understanding the needs of hosts and guests and collaborating closely with our operations, legal, business, design, and product teams. The policies you build will directly shape how millions of hosts and guests experience Airbnb and their confidence in the platform.

About You

  • You are a seasoned policy leader who loves solving complex problems and collaborating cross-functionally.
  • You have deep expertise in the anti-discrimination space and a track record in safety policies addressing real-world harms.
  • You are an excellent communicator with exceptional writing skills.
  • You are an adept presenter with experience engaging with all levels of leadership, including senior executives.
  • You are a team player who thrives in a fast-moving environment and brings a strategic mindset and bias toward execution.
  • You are principled, have meticulous attention to detail, and incorporate diverse perspectives in pursuit of the best decisions and outcomes possible.
  • You are experienced at developing and implementing policies and measuring their effectiveness.
  • You are proactively data-driven: you don't wait for problems to surface — you seek out data, research, and insights to identify gaps and opportunities to improve policies before they become issues.

A Typical Day: 

  • Have broad ownership over our policies affecting trust in Airbnb, especially in the anti-discrimination and safety space
  • Lead policy development and draft clear and scalable policy frameworks that keep pace with company priorities
  • Foster, build, and maintain relationships with cross-functional stakeholders across the business including Operations, Legal, Anti-Discrimination and Equity, Public Policy, Product, Communications, and Supply, acting as a trusted policy partner who helps teams move forward

title: Senior Systems Engineer, BizTech
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The world is changing how it works; not just in where we do it, but in how fast and how well we can do it. Airbnb has already shown that we can move with speed and intention.  We navigated a pandemic, rebuilt our company from the ground up, had a successful IPO, and shipped product upgrades – all while working remotely. That experience didn't just change where we work. It changed what we believe is possible.

Now, a new shift is underway. AI is fundamentally changing the leverage available to every team – compressing timelines, breaking down traditional job description silos, raising the ceiling on quality, and enabling small, focused groups to accomplish what once required much larger ones. At Airbnb, we are not treating AI as a future consideration. We are moving fast to embed it into how we operate today – using it to multiply the impact of every employee, every system, and decisions we make every day. The companies and teams that embrace this shift with urgency and discipline will define what's possible in the years ahead. We intend to be one of them.

Collaboration Products

The Collaboration Products team owns the enterprise systems that Airbnb's workforce relies on to plan, build, and deliver — including our Atlassian ecosystem, AI-powered tooling integrations, and custom-built engineering platforms. Our mission goes beyond keeping the lights on. We are moving fast to modernize our stack, retire technical debt, and integrate AI capabilities that directly multiply the productivity and quality of the teams we serve. We build with urgency, operate with rigor, and treat every system we touch as an opportunity to raise the bar on what BizTech delivers to Airbnb.

The Difference You Will Make:

The Senior Systems Engineer is a hands-on technical leader who moves fast, builds to last, and uses AI as a force multiplier — not a future initiative. In this role, you will own the configuration, migration, and continuous improvement of Airbnb's Atlassian platforms, including leading the active deprecation of Jira Data Center and full transition to Jira Cloud. But your impact goes beyond administration. You will identify where AI and automation can compress delivery cycles, reduce toil, and improve the quality and reliability of the systems our workforce depends on — and then build those improvements, quickly. You bring the platform depth to architect scalable solutions and the judgment to know when to move fast and when to be deliberate. You are the kind of engineer who raises the velocity and quality of everyone around you.

A Typical Day: 

  • Serve as the primary SME and hands-on administrator for JiraCloud Software, JiraCloud Service Management (JSM), and associated Atlassian tooling; own configuration standards, governance, and technical debt reduction across the environment
  • Architect and implement scalable Jira configurations including custom workflows, issue type hierarchies, permission schemes, notification schemes, screens, and field configurations aligned with Atlassian best practices
  • Lead and execute Jira migrations - including Data Center to Cloud - coordinating with cross-functional stakeholders to deliver seamless cutover experiences
  • Design and configure Jira Service Management projects including SLAs, custom queues, JSM Forms, approval workflows, and security schemes to support internal service delivery teams
  • Build and maintain advanced analytics, dashboards, and reporting solutions using native tooling for Jira Cloud as a first line of options;  Airbnb has elected to avoid Atlassian Marketplace products for information security, privacy & legal prerogatives.   Airbnb is building custom Forge applications that will require your ongoing maintenance and partnership with supporting systems engineering teams.
  • Configure and administer Atlassian access management, user lifecycle management, license tier optimization, and security posture improvements
  • Evaluate if Atlassian Marketplace plugins architecture evolves to a point where Airbnb could consider adopting plugins where business needs dictate, and where security, legal, and privacy requirements are satisfied.
  • Act as a strategic partner to business stakeholders by leading requirements-gathering sessions, translating business needs into technical designs, and proactively identifying opportunities for automation and process improvement
  • Configure and expand Atlassian Rovo AI agents and automation rules; evaluate emerging AI/ML capabilities within the Atlassian ecosystem and champion responsible, contextually appropriate AI adoption aligned with Airbnb's mission
  • Write and maintain custom automation rules using Jira's native Automation engine and JavaScript; leverage Jira REST API for integrations, data imports, and custom reporting
  • Lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) efforts for platform changes and migrations; develop and maintain test plans, test scripts, and defect tracking documentation
  • Facilitate Agile ceremonies (sprint planning, retrospectives, standups) as needed; operate as Scrum Master or Product Owner for platform-focused workstreams
  • Document system configurations, runbooks, and knowledge base articles to support operational continuity and enable self-service across the organization
  • Participate in on-call rotation and provide escalation support for critical Atlassian platform issues


Your Expertise:

  • 7+ years of hands-on Atlassian administration experience, including Jira Software, Jira Service Management (across JiraCloud & JiraDC) in enterprise environments with large user populations
  • Deep expertise in Jira workflow design, including post functions, validators, conditions, and custom properties; strong command of JQL for filters, subscriptions, dashboards, and board configuration
  • Proven experience leading Jira migrations (Data Center to Cloud), including project configuration migration, macro compatibility, and data integrity validation
  • Experience configuring and administering Jira Cloud native tooling for capacity planning and portfolio reporting

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Risk Tools & Automation Lead
descriptionHtml:

About the Company

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to millions of hosts who have welcomed guests in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

The Payments Risk Operations team protects Airbnb's guests, hosts, and the platform from fraud, financial loss, and abuse. Our investigators and agents review high-risk activity every day, and the quality of their tools directly shapes the speed, accuracy, and consistency of every decision they make. You will join a team of operators, analysts, and program leaders who partner closely with Platform, Engineering, Data Science, Design, and Legal to keep our community safe.

The Difference You Will Make

As the Senior Risk Tools & Automation Lead, you will own the end-to-end agent experience for risk and fraud operations. You will define what our investigators need, design and conceptualize the next generation of the risk workbench, and drive automation through process efficiencies and AI. You will be the voice of the agent in tooling decisions and the bridge between operational reality and technical execution. Your work will reduce manual effort, shorten handle times, improve decision quality, and free our experts to focus on the most complex cases.

A Typical Day

Agent experience

  • Own the end-to-end agent experience across risk and fraud investigation workflows, from case intake through decision, documentation, and quality review.
  • Spend time with agents to observe workflows, map pain points, and quantify friction in handle time, clicks, context switching, and error rates.
  • Establish feedback loops (surveys, office hours, champion networks, ticket intake) so agent needs are captured, prioritized, and closed out transparently.
  • Partner with Training, Quality, and Workforce Management to ensure tooling changes land with clear enablement, documentation, and adoption tracking.

Tooling requirements and improvements

  • Translate operational needs into clear, prioritized business requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria that Platform and Engineering can build against.
  • Own and manage the operational risk tooling roadmap and backlog, balancing quick wins, foundational investments, and policy or regulatory needs.
  • Lead intake, triage, and prioritization of tooling requests using impact sizing (time saved, loss prevented, accuracy gained, risk reduced).
  • Drive user acceptance testing (UAT), launch readiness, and post-launch measurement for every tooling release.

Workbench design and conceptualization

  • Define the long-term vision for a unified risk workbench that brings signals, account history, payment data, linked entities, and decisioning into a single, intuitive workspace.
  • Partner with Platform, Design, and UX Research to run discovery, build journey maps, create wireframes and prototypes, and conduct usability testing with agents.
  • Champion design principles of simplicity, consistency, and accessibility so agents can make accurate decisions quickly and confidently.

Automation through efficiencies and AI

  • Identify, size, and prioritize automation opportunities across manual and repetitive work, including case routing, data gathering, enrichment, summarization, and low-risk decisioning.
  • Partner with Platform, Engineering, and Data Science to design and deploy AI-assisted capabilities such as case summaries, recommended actions, agent copilots, and automated documentation.
  • Define human-in-the-loop guardrails, quality controls, and monitoring so automation improves efficiency without compromising accuracy, fairness, or compliance.
  • Build business cases that tie automation to measurable outcomes and report progress to senior leadership.

Cross-functional leadership

  • Serve as the primary operations policy partner to Platform, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Policy, Legal, Compliance, and Finance on all risk tooling initiatives.
  • Influence without authority, align technical and non-technical stakeholders on priorities, tradeoffs, and timelines.
  • Communicate roadmaps, launches, and impact clearly to audiences ranging from frontline agents to executive leadership.

Your Expertise

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in operations, program management, or product management.
  • 5+ years of experience in fraud, payment risk, trust and safety, or a related investigations industry.
  • Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred.
  • Proven track record of writing successful business requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria that led to shipped tools with measurable impact.
  • Familiarity with user experience testing and design, including discovery interviews, journey mapping, usability testing, and working from wireframes or prototypes.
  • Demonstrated success in cross-functional collaboration with both technical partners (Engineering, Data Science, Platform) and non-technical partners (Operations, Legal, Compliance, Finance).
  • Experience identifying and delivering automation or process efficiency improvements at scale, with results tied to metrics such as handle time, throughput, accuracy, or loss.
  • Strong analytical skills, with comfort using data to size opportunities, build business cases, and measure outcomes (SQL or similar skills a plus).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to simplify complex technical and operational concepts for executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience designing or launching agent workbenches, case management systems, or investigation consoles.
  • Experience applying generative AI or large language models in operational settings, such as agent copilots, case summarization, or automated decision support.
  • Working knowledge of fraud and risk domains such as payment fraud, chargebacks, account takeover, identity verification, or AML.
  • Familiarity with workflow and automation platforms (for example, rules engines, RPA, or low-code tools) and with agile delivery practices.
  • Experience leading change management and driving adoption across large, globally distributed operations teams.
  • Experience working at an e-commerce, travel, fintech, or payments company.

title: Senior Manager, Business Technology Enablement
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join: 

We are looking for a Senior Manager to lead BizTech Enablement and Innovation (BEI), BizTech's solutions partner to the rest of the company. BEI works with Finance, Legal, People, Marketing, Global Operations, Policy and Communications, Design, and other non-technical functions to understand how they work, turn their problems into working solutions, and make sure employees know about and adopt the technology BizTech provides. The team also brings what it learns back to BizTech product teams and vendors to shape their roadmaps. You will report to the Director, Tech Foundations.

The Difference You Will Make:

This is a strategic leadership role within a large business unit. For the next 18 months, the team's focus is AI. You will own the company's approach to AI adoption and impact outside of Engineering, set the vision for AI-enabled work, hold functions accountable to measurable outcomes, and serve as BizTech's primary partner to E-Team leaders on AI transformation.

More broadly, you will lead how Airbnb's non-technical functions discover, adopt, and get value from business technology. That covers quick consultations and fast-track solutions, go-to-market for new BizTech services, and building or buying new solutions where existing tools fall short. In the near term, you will define where Airbnb should be on AI-enabled work in two years, build the team and partnerships to get there, and make the trade-offs required to deliver it.

Success in this role is measured in business outcomes, not tool rollouts: functions that have redesigned their work around technology and AI, defined their own impact metrics, and can show the efficiency and quality gains, supported by a simpler tool landscape with fewer duplicate and unsupported tools.

A Typical Day: 

Set strategy and vision

  • Help define and own the multi-year strategy for AI adoption and impact across Airbnb's non-technical functions, aligned with company and Tech priorities.
  • Assess current gaps, existing capabilities, and emerging AI trends to anticipate how functions will need to work 18 to 24 months out, and translate that into a roadmap and investment.
    Simplify the tools business teams use by steering them to supported solutions and closing the gaps that lead them to find their own.
  • Set organizational OKRs and success criteria for near and long-term initiatives, and hold teams and partners accountable for delivery.
  • Make and communicate hard trade-offs across competing functional demands, platform constraints, and budget.

Drive executive alignment and function-level accountability

  • Serve as the senior BizTech partner to leadership teams on AI transformation, including regular readouts to executives and senior Tech leadership.
  • Establish the framework by which each function defines, measures, and reports the business impact of AI, and drive adoption of that framework as a standard.
  • Build a metric-driven accountability culture: clear baselines, targets, and ownership for every function, with a single trusted source of truth for adoption and impact data.
  • Tailor narratives for different audiences, from detailed methodology with data and engineering partners to concise decision framing for executives.
  • Seek feedback from partner teams and use it to improve delivery; raise risks to leadership early.
  • Listen actively and anticipate where change will meet resistance.

Build the operating model and ecosystem

  • Design and continuously refine the operating model that connects different technical functions and networks into one coordinated enablement system.
  • Shape the enablement approach for AI usage so functions can build and share AI solutions at scale.
  • Partner with platform and product teams to influence the AI tooling roadmap based on the needs of non-technical users.
  • Direct external partner and consulting engagements, including scope, governance, and return on investment.
  • Set quality, reliability, and security standards for the AI solutions the team and functions build; own operational issues in production and drive the fixes that prevent repeats.
  • Make sure tech debt and the long-term upkeep of shipped solutions are prioritized across the team’s roadmap.

Lead and grow the organization

  • Lead a multi-disciplinary, globally distributed organization including managers, Business Solutions Engineers, Systems Architects, and Program Managers.
  • Create a team environment that values constructive debate, risk-taking, and learning from experiments, and that fosters belonging across regions.
  • Build an 18+ month talent plan and a succession pipeline, including hiring at L10 and above.
  • Coach, mentor, and grow the team to communicate clearly, resolve conflict early, and build inclusive teams.

Champion innovation and continuous improvement

  • Pilot new technologies, including AI, with business teams, and hand proven solutions to product owners for long-term support.
  • Coach leaders across functions to connect AI capabilities to business value.
  • Establish mechanisms that turn learnings from individual functions into reusable patterns across the company.

Cultural and functional excellence

  • Represent BizTech in company-wide AI forums and contribute to hiring committees, talent processes, and Airbnb's internal AI community.
  • Role model Airbnb's core values and strengthen the company's mission through the way AI is introduced to employees.

Your Expertise:

  • 12+ years of industry experience in business technology, enterprise systems, digital transformation, or technical program leadership, including 5+ years leading managers and multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Demonstrated track record setting and delivering multi-year strategy for a company-wide technology or transformation program with executive visibility.
  • Experience leading business technology consulting, solutions engineering, or IT business partnering for non-technical teams, including influencing product and vendor roadmaps.
  • Experience owning the quality, reliability, and support of technology solutions in production.
  • Experience building trusted relationships with, and influencing, C-level and E-Team executives, including the ability to align or challenge senior leaders on priorities.
  • Deep, hands-on understanding of generative AI tools and agentic workflows, and how they change the nature of non-technical work.
  • Strong analytical judgment: able to define measurement frameworks, interpret adoption and impact data, and ensure data quality and credibility at an executive level.
  • Proven ability to lead through ambiguity and rapid change, including shifting org structures, evolving technology, and competing priorities.
  • Experience designing operating models across multiple teams and organizations without direct authority.
  • Experience attracting, hiring, and developing senior talent and managers across regions.
  • Preferred: experience leading enterprise AI adoption or change management at a large technology company.
  • Preferred: experience managing external consulting partners and globally distributed teams.
  • Preferred: ability to travel as needed, approximately 10 to 20%.

title: Business Operations and Growth Lead - DACH & CEE
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. The Community You Will Join

Help shape the next chapter of Airbnb's growth across DACH & Central and Eastern Europe.

We're looking for a Business Operations and Growth Lead to join our Berlin team, working closely with the Country Manager and territory leadership team to drive business performance, shape market strategy and unlock new growth opportunities.

Operating at the intersection of strategy, analytics and execution, you'll turn complex marketplace challenges into actionable insights and measurable business outcomes.

You'll thrive in this role if you're commercially minded, analytically strong and entrepreneurial, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity and turn ambitious ideas into results.

The Difference You Will Make

As a strategic partner to the Country Manager, you'll play a key role in shaping and delivering growth across DACH & CEE, with exposure to EMEA and global initiatives.

  • Drive market strategy: Identify growth opportunities across supply, demand, pricing and evolving regulatory landscapes.
  • Lead advanced analytics: Build sophisticated models, forecasts and business cases from scratch, translating complex data into actionable commercial recommendations.
  • Own business performance: Analyse marketplace trends, lead performance reviews and identify the drivers behind growth, risks and opportunities.
  • Drive strategic priorities: Lead territory OKRs, business planning and execution against ambitious growth targets.
  • Influence and deliver: Align cross-functional leaders, challenge thinking and drive results without formal authority.
  • Scale what works: Lead market initiatives, pilot new ideas and adapt EMEA and global programs for local impact.

A Typical Day

Set priorities and strategy

  • Develop integrated territory strategies based on marketplace dynamics (supply, demand and pricing), business needs, opportunities presented by the ever-changing regulatory landscape and previous learnings
  • Lead the territory's OKR program: define the key objectives and priorities with the Country Manager and all cross-functional teams, identify roadblocks and collaborate with OKR owners on performance improvements

Deliver actionable business analysis

  • Build the analysis and frameworks that support territory decisions, from supply and demand balance to pricing, in collaboration with FP&A and Data Science, deep dive into areas of strength and weakness, and present actionable plans to leadership
  • Own the territory's business performance reviews: prepare and present the Monthly and Quarterly Business Reviews and the daily and weekly performance updates, proactively flag opportunities and risks, and initiate the deep dives that follow

Lead with operational rigor and discipline

  • Run the day-to-day operating cadence of the territory's cross-functional leadership team: set the agenda, align functions on shared priorities, drive follow-through and resolve trade-offs openly
  • Run the planning and budgeting processes, including big bet proposals, tracking spend and performance against plan
  • Build a strong global network of stakeholders across functions and partner with them to identify opportunities for the territory

Your Expertise

  • 8-10 years of relevant work experience with a strong analytical background and a broad business understanding across functions, including marketing and operations, and a solid grasp of marketplace mechanics (how supply, demand and pricing interact)
  • Experience in a consumer tech or marketplace business, ideally in a two-sided marketplace such as online travel, mobility, delivery or hospitality, and/or at a top tier consulting/private equity/investment banking firm, in a capacity where you worked cross-functionally and across diverse teams to influence change, ideally leading peers without direct authority in a matrix
  • A strong written and verbal communicator, comfortable presenting to senior leadership
  • Proven track record as a hands-on business analyst: you build models, business cases and forecasts from scratch in Excel and use AI tools to analyse faster and go deeper; SQL and Python knowledge is a plus
  • Near-native English and working knowledge of German

Location

The role is based in Berlin, Germany. Presence in the Berlin office several days a week is critical for close collaboration with the Country Manager and the cross-functional teams.

descriptionHtml:

The Community you will join:

The Cities team leads the work necessary to implement the regulatory products and processes needed globally to comply with regulations, and does so in a manner that also sustainably supports Airbnb’s growth.

The difference you will make:

As a Regulatory Operations Lead, you will bring specialized experience in regulatory operations, expertise in team management and the ability to advise and guide cross-functional teams across geographies based on trends and observations to continuously evolve our long term strategy. You will lead with influence, build structure through ambiguity, and deliver innovation that enables scalable, elegant solutions.

You will be responsible for driving the delivery of centrally run strategic programs, while also defining and executing localized strategies that play a key role in accelerating Airbnb's growth and retention efforts. You should be comfortable developing operational programs and processes, have experience navigating complex regulatory environments, and possess a keen eye for quality/detail that inspires the teams and individuals you work with to exceed expectations.  

A typical day: 

  • Lead the strategic development and execution of highly scalable regulatory programs across multiple jurisdictions, effectively communicating outcomes and insights to senior leadership.
  • Lead end-to-end execution of complex regulatory programs, ensuring measurable outcomes, sustainable operations, and readiness to meet evolving legal requirements while ensuring Airbnb’s obligations are met with excellence.
  • Manage a high performing team of individuals responsible for strategy and regulatory operations.
  • Translate emerging regulatory trends into actionable business strategies for senior leadership. 
  • Partner with cross-functional technical partners to design solutions that enable proactive, automated compliance solutions.
  • Identify and lead resolution of regulatory risks or incidents, coordinating with legal and policy counterparts to develop mitigation and escalation strategies.
  • Influence cross-functional roadmaps and corporate strategy through deep expertise in regulatory frameworks.
  • Serve as the primary liaison and operational architect for your jurisdictions, establishing operational rhythms and ensuring alignment among cross-functional stakeholders while maintaining comprehensive project documentation.
  • Drive high-impact strategic projects aimed at enhancing efficiency and effectiveness while also aligning with broader business goals.
  • Lead the strategic development and execution of scalable regulatory products and programs across multiple jurisdictions, effectively communicating outcomes and insights to senior leadership.
  • Analyze data by running queries and creating dashboards to identify trends, surface anomalies, and perform the necessary investigation

Your expertise: 

  • 10+ years of experience in regulatory operations, legal/policy compliance, consulting, project management, or related fields.
  • Strong team management skills and the ability to coach and mentor direct reports. 
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and lead multiple projects in a fast-paced and complex regulatory environment.
  • Experience building scalable technical solutions and processes to mitigate regulatory risks. 
  • Experience designing and operationalizing regulatory workflows.
  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex regulatory information as applicable and required for varied audiences.
  • Comfortable and skilled at regularly interfacing with, influencing and being a thought partner to senior management to inform strategy and decision-making, yielding positive outcomes.
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with a track record of aligning cross-functional teams to achieve business objectives.

title: Senior Communications Manager, Korea
descriptionHtml:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join: 

The Airbnb Communications team is responsible for telling Airbnb’s story around the world. 

We help drive consideration and usage of our products and services in addition to generating buzz, supporting the legitimization of our community, and promoting trust in our brand. We lead the communications strategy to make Airbnb synonymous with magical travel and the world’s leading platform for hospitality entrepreneurs. 

We speak to the media, influencers, hosts and guests, industry commentators, thought leaders and the wider community - we are the voice of Airbnb. We’re a fast growing, high-energy team with a passion for people, places and great stories. If you’d like to be part of one of the world’s greatest teams, come tell us your story.

The Difference You Will Make:

We are hiring a Senior Communications Manager for Korea. This role leads policy and corporate reputation communications in Korea. It identifies and develops the key issues and narratives that shape how Airbnb is understood by media, policymakers and the public, builds the relationships beyond the newsroom that give those narratives weight, including the host community, academia, think tanks, and industry and professional associations, and runs the ‘always on’ press office that keeps Airbnb visible and accurately represented in Korean media every day. 

The role works closely with the Korea Communications team members and cross-functional partners to make sure Airbnb’s position on the issues that matter in Korea is clear, credible and heard. It also provides press strategy and media counsel for consumer campaigns led by the wider team, so that those moments strengthen Airbnb’s reputation as well.

We’re looking for a seasoned communications professional with strong judgment on policy and reputation issues, a strong grasp of the Korean news and regulatory landscape, the ability to turn complex topics into clear narratives, and the relationship skills to engage journalists and external stakeholders with credibility. Disciplined on the daily basics, strategic on the issues that count. 

The role is based in Seoul and reports to the Senior Communications Lead, Korea.

A Typical Day:

  • Lead policy and corporate reputation communications in Korea, shaping the team’s strategy on key issues and turning it into plans and delivery.
  • Develop narratives that shape how Airbnb is understood by media, policymakers and the public, including short-term rental regulation, trust and safety, corporate reputation, thought leadership, and Airbnb’s economic and community contribution.
  • Develop messaging, holding statements, Q&A, and executive briefing materials on key corporate issues, and lead reactive media handling in partnership with the Public Policy team.
  • Build relationships beyond the media that lend credibility to Airbnb’s narratives, including host community representatives, academics, think tanks, industry and professional associations, and local government, and drive third-party partnerships such as research, forums and speaking opportunities that put Airbnb’s issues on the public agenda.
  • Lead spokesperson preparation for media interviews, public speaking and stakeholder engagements. 
  • Strategize and run the ‘always on’ press office with local agencies: daily monitoring and issue flagging, proactive data and trend pitches, inbound media handling, and a steady drumbeat of host and community stories.
  • Build and maintain core relationships with reporters across policy, business, economy, tech and travel beats, and manage the journalist database and media engagement calendar.
  • Set press strategy and provide media counsel for for consumer campaigns, and localise global campaigns and launches into Korea-appropriate press materials, so campaign moments also strengthen reputation and avoid issue risk.
  • Run Communications team operations in Korea: agency and vendor management, budgets, purchase orders and payments, planning cadences, and compliance with financial policies and key processes.
  • Own measurement and reporting: set and track KPIs, run coverage and sentiment analysis, and deliver regular data-based reports to local and regional stakeholders.

Your Expertise:

  • At least 8 years communications or public affairs experience in an agency, in-house or public sector role; preference to those with experience working with global tech/ platform/ travel brands
  • Strong understanding of the Korean media and regulatory landscape, with an established network of journalist contacts across relevant fields.
  • Ability to turn complex regulatory or data-heavy topics into clear, credible narratives and written materials such as messaging, Q&A, op-eds and briefings, with good judgment and composure on sensitive issues and reactive media situations
  • Experience engaging stakeholders beyond the media, such as community groups, academia, think tanks, industry associations or government
  • Proven ability to work collaboratively with multi-functional leads in a matrix organization, in particular with Public Policy
